solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Henry tucked into piece of cake and currently hot toast

indicators.note: something tucked into a thing sits inside it, so one part goes within another

blocks.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
a cinch is something very easy, as is a piece of cake
what is hot right now is in, as in fashion

explanation.surface: Someone describes their tea: a slice of cake and some toast fresh from the grill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toast' looks like bread in this breakfast picture, but it is the drink-raising kind. 'Hot' as trendy is a common way to clue IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Chin-chin is an old-fashioned British salutation said when raising glasses before drinking together.

clue.text: Raphael maybe entertained by game that’s fixed

indicators.note: a host who entertains a guest has them inside the house, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: chess is a board game
Raphael is one of the archangels; 'maybe' marks him as an example

explanation.surface: An art lover suspects the painter Raphael was the guest at a rigged game.
explanation.walkthrough: Raphael reads as the Renaissance painter, but here he is the archangel of the Bible and Book of Tobit.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unchanging or permanently set in place is fixed; the words are straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: Problem generated by Iago’s opening lines

indicators.note: an opening is where something begins, so only the first letter is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of Iago
L is the abbreviation for line, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A theatre critic blames the trouble in Othello on the lines Iago speaks at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening lines' looks like a single phrase about a play's first speech; split it, and 'opening' works on Iago while 'lines' gives two Ls.
explanation.definitionFit: An ill is a noun for a trouble or misfortune, as in the ills of society.

clue.text: In unsophisticated fashion clothing from couturier, equally foxy

indicators.note: clothing is what is worn on the outside, so only the outer letters are kept

blocks.note: the first and last letters of couturier
as in 'as big as', meaning to the same degree
a foxy person is cunning or sly

explanation.surface: A fashion writer sneers at a crude outfit from a designer that is also rather foxy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' and 'clothing' make it all about dress, yet fashion belongs to the definition and clothing marks the edges of couturier.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting crassly means behaving without refinement or taste, which is doing things in an unsophisticated manner.

clue.text: Working with assignment following pay cut

indicators.note: cutting something shortens it, so the last letter is lost
one thing following another comes after it, so this piece is placed second

blocks.note: income is pay; cut short it loses its final E
a mission is a task someone is assigned

explanation.surface: An employee takes on a new assignment despite having had their salary reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like an office grievance about pay cuts, but 'cut' only trims one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship or machine in commission is in active service and operating properly, which is to say working.

clue.text: Groups aboard boats picked up sail

indicators.note: to pick something up is to hear it, as a radio picks up a signal, so this is about sound

blocks.note: the teams working on ships are crews

explanation.surface: Passengers or crews on board ships hoisting a sail that has been pulled from the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' sounds like hauling a sail aboard, but here it means heard.
explanation.definitionFit: To cruise is to travel by ship at an easy pace, so the verb sail fits it.

clue.text: Artist cheers rubbish noise made by rapper

blocks.note: RA, Royal Academician, a standard crossword artist
ta is British slang for thanks, as is cheers
tat is cheap worthless stuff

explanation.surface: A musician's fans cheer while critics dismiss a rap artist's output as rubbish noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rapper' looks like a hip-hop artist, but it is a door knocker, and its noise is a sharp knocking.
explanation.definitionFit: Rat-a-tat imitates the repeated sound of knocking on a door, the sound a knocker makes.

clue.text: I look to seize writers with love for Homer or Milton’s work

indicators.note: to seize something is to grasp it, so one piece holds others inside

blocks.note: taken as it stands
lo is an old word meaning look or behold
pens are writing implements
Eros was the Greek god of love, fitting Homer's Greek world

explanation.surface: A poet grabs some fellow authors and lovingly swaps Homer's epics for Milton's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Homer' tempts toward the epic poet's own works, but he only flags that the love wanted is the Greek god's name. LO is an archaic interjection.
explanation.definitionFit: Il Penseroso is a pastoral poem by John Milton, companion piece to L'Allegro, so an example of his writing.

clue.text: Top children’s toy to create current disturbance

indicators.note: to top something is to cut off its head, so in a down answer the first letter goes

blocks.note: a teddy bear, minus its first letter

explanation.surface: A popular children's toy is so exciting it causes a disturbance among shoppers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like an adjective meaning best-selling, but it is a verb meaning behead. 'Current' is a flow of water, not a present-day row.
explanation.definitionFit: An eddy is a swirl in running water that goes against the main flow, a disturbance in a stream.

clue.text: Daughter forsakes trifling romance for marriage

indicators.note: to forsake is to abandon, so this letter leaves the word

blocks.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
a dalliance is a casual, unserious love affair

explanation.surface: A daughter gives up a casual fling in favour of settling down and marrying.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a tidy family story; underneath, D simply drops off the front of DALLIANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance is a union, and historically a marriage joining two families is described that way.

clue.text: Retiring policeman’s maintaining place without much upstairs

indicators.note: to maintain is to keep and hold, so one piece is held within another
retiring means going back, so the whole thing runs backwards

blocks.note: DI, Detective Inspector, with the 's
to place something is to put it

explanation.surface: A detective on the point of retirement keeps a flat with no upper floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upstairs' seems to belong with the house, but 'not much upstairs' is an idiom for having little in the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Having nothing much upstairs is a colloquial idiom for lacking brains, so it means dim or unintelligent.

clue.text: Consider cutting endless red tape, oddly, to be most important

indicators.note: without an end, a word loses its final letter
done oddly means done in a strange way, so the letters are rearranged
something that cuts into another goes into its middle, so one piece sits inside

blocks.note: to ponder is to think over
red without its last letter
taken as it stands

explanation.surface: An official decides that slashing bureaucracy, strange as it seems, should be the top priority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red tape' reads as one idea, bureaucracy, but must be split; 'oddly' suggests taking odd letters, yet here it scrambles.
explanation.definitionFit: To preponderate is to outweigh everything else in power or influence, being dominant or of greatest weight.

clue.text: He unexpectedly helped a parent aboard cargo train in motion

indicators.note: something in motion is moving around, so the letters are shifted about
a passenger who is aboard is inside the vehicle, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: goods are freight or cargo
taken as it stands
ma is mother
anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A man surprisingly lent a hand to a mother climbing onto a moving freight train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cargo train' suggests a British goods train; GOODS plus the scrambled TRAIN form the carriage that A MA boards.
explanation.definitionFit: In the parable in Luke, the Samaritan unexpectedly aided a beaten traveller whom others ignored.

clue.text: He wanted more surprising end, say, after finale of concerto on organ

indicators.note: a finale is the ending, so the last letter is kept
one thing after another comes later, so this piece is placed last

blocks.note: the last letter of concerto
the liver is a body organ
a twist is a surprise ending, 'say' marks it as an example

explanation.surface: A listener wished a concerto had a more surprising close after the organ's finale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' sounds musical with 'concerto' beside it, but it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's orphan famously asks for more gruel in the workhouse, the best-known line of the novel.

clue.text: Suffer anxiety over correct pronunciation guide

indicators.note: in a down answer, over means placed above, so this piece comes first

blocks.note: to stress is to worry
a teacher marks or corrects work

explanation.surface: A language learner frets about saying words right and turns to a guide.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'correct' an adjective about proper speech; it is a verb, the teacher's job.
explanation.definitionFit: A stress mark is the accent symbol in a dictionary telling readers which syllable carries emphasis.

clue.text: Abridged books containing article by unknown amateurs

indicators.note: one thing containing another holds it inside, so a piece goes within

blocks.note: lit, short for literature
the indefinite article
algebra's unknowns are x, y and z

explanation.surface: Shortened editions featuring an essay by anonymous amateur authors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abridged' looks like a publishing term for the whole books, but it tells you to shorten the word literature.
explanation.definitionFit: The laity are people without professional or specialist expertise, the lay public, so non-experts.

clue.text: Like a bad waiter’s tip I meant to revise

indicators.note: revising something reworks it, so the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, nine letters

explanation.surface: A diner reconsiders the gratuity they meant to leave for poor restaurant service.
explanation.walkthrough: The waiter here is not in a restaurant: it is anyone who waits, and a bad one cannot bear to.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone poor at waiting for things lacks patience, so a bad waiter in this literal sense is restless.

clue.text: Scottish writer, odd figure hoarding Time back numbers

indicators.note: to hoard is to keep something stored away, so one piece is held inside
going back means running in the other direction

blocks.note: seven is an odd number
T is the abbreviation for time
NOS is short for numbers

explanation.surface: An eccentric Scottish author squirrels away old back issues of a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd figure' pretends to be a strange person; it is a number. 'Time back numbers' looks like old issues of the magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Louis Stevenson, author of Treasure Island and Kidnapped, was born in Edinburgh.

clue.text: Like horse, tailless bovid’s in biannual event

indicators.note: without a tail, a word loses its final letter

blocks.note: equine means horse-like, here without its last letter
an ox is a member of the cattle family

explanation.surface: A cow or antelope without a tail appears in a twice-yearly show, looking rather horse-like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailless' seems to describe the animal but acts on the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: The equinox, when day and night are equal, occurs twice every year, in March and September.

clue.text: Fine in case of bigger drug bust

indicators.note: a case is the outside of something, so only the outer letters are kept
one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: the first and last letters of bigger
E is ecstasy
OK means fine

explanation.surface: A penalty in a case involving a larger police raid on narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine', 'case' and 'drug bust' all sound like a courtroom; bust is actually the definition, meaning penniless.
explanation.definitionFit: Going bust and being broke are both informal ways of saying having no money left at all.

clue.text: Sang and wittered on with Liberal in higher position

indicators.note: moved into a higher position, a letter is shifted upward and the order changes

blocks.note: to babble is to chatter on at length
L for Liberal, already in the word; it names the letter that moves and adds none

explanation.surface: A politician sang and rambled on alongside a Liberal colleague who had been promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: The L already in BABBLED moves up, which in a down answer means earlier, from fifth place to second.
explanation.definitionFit: To sing, in criminal slang, is to inform to the police, as does anyone who blabs a secret.

clue.text: Trip runners poorer at running through French city

indicators.note: something running is in motion, so the letters move about
passing through something means being inside it, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: Tours is a city on the Loire
anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Athletes jogging through a French city trip over, their times getting poorer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trip runners' looks like athletes who stumble; it is companies that organise trips.
explanation.definitionFit: Tour operators organise and run package holidays, which are trips, so they are trip organisers.

clue.text: Heir of Isaac Hayes auditioning covers

indicators.note: a thing that covers another conceals it, so the letters lie within these words

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: The soul singer Isaac Hayes performs cover versions at an audition.
explanation.walkthrough: Isaac Hayes is the soul singer; 'Isaac' does double duty, leading the definition to the biblical Isaac.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Esau was the elder son of Isaac and so his rightful heir before Jacob took the blessing.

clue.text: Broadcaster screens current news free of padding

indicators.note: a screen shields what lies behind it, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: Sky is a British satellite broadcaster
what is current is in, fashionable now
news is what is new, and new abbreviates to N

explanation.surface: A TV channel airs the latest bulletin stripped of all filler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Padding' looks like filler in a news report, but it means body fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Skinny describes a very thin person, one with no fat or flesh cushioning their frame.

clue.text: Yogi perhaps follows American behind capital city

indicators.note: one thing that follows another comes after it, so this piece goes second

blocks.note: can is American slang for the buttocks
Yogi Berra, the New York Yankees baseball catcher, 'perhaps' marks an example

explanation.surface: A yogi trails behind an American tourist through a capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yogi' suggests a practitioner of yoga, or the cartoon bear; it is the baseball player famous for sayings.
explanation.definitionFit: Canberra is the purpose-built seat of government of Australia, its national capital.

clue.text: Friend of Winnie’s runs round and round

blocks.note: R is runs in cricket scoring
each round is the letter O, a circle

explanation.surface: A friend of someone named Winnie jogs in circles.
explanation.walkthrough: Winnie is Winnie-the-Pooh, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Roo is the young kangaroo in A.A. Milne's stories, a companion of Pooh Bear in the Hundred Acre Wood.

clue.text: You dictated right extension for original document

indicators.note: dictated words are spoken to be written down, so this concerns sound

blocks.note: the letter name is said the same way
RT is an abbreviation for right
ext. is the short form used in phone numbers

explanation.surface: A boss dictates a telephone extension so a copy of the original can be sent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extension' is a phone line, whose abbreviation is familiar from office directories.
explanation.definitionFit: An urtext is the earliest version of a text, from which later editions are derived, a German-derived term.

clue.text: Hold cake and hold bananas

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters go wild and reorder

blocks.note: anagram fodder, without the joining word

explanation.surface: Instructions for carrying a picnic: keep the cake and the bananas in your hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' seems to be food alongside cake; it is slang for mad. 'And' joins the fodder words and is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A headlock is a wrestling grip around the opponent's neck, a type of hold in that sport.
